Hi. I have a question about the real privacy we have with BTCs. I can't find a clear answer so maybe you can help me. I want to start using BTC (the first reason is supporting project and services like voat anonymously) and the most famous platform seems to be Coinbase, which is often recommended in forums. But they ask for a lot of private info for account completion before being able to buy BTCs. From bitcoin.org :

Bitcoin works with an unprecedented level of transparency that most people are not used to dealing with. All Bitcoin transactions are public, traceable, and permanently stored in the Bitcoin network. Bitcoin addresses are the only information used to define where bitcoins are allocated and where they are sent. These addresses are created privately by each user's wallets. However, once addresses are used, they become tainted by the history of all transactions they are involved with. Anyone can see the balance and all transactions of any address. Since users usually have to reveal their identity in order to receive services or goods, Bitcoin addresses cannot remain fully anonymous. For these reasons, Bitcoin addresses should only be used once and users must be careful not to disclose their addresses.

So if I (for instance) want to make a donation to voat anonymously, I would have to complete the Coinbase account (and thus giving my real ID, phone number and so on...), then transfer BTCs to another wallet and the use this wallet to make my donation ? But as my transactions are public, I'm theoretically traceable whatever I do, even with an infinite number of intermediate wallets between Coinbase and the anon transaction I want to make. Can BTCs be fully anonymous somehow ?

If anyone has a good answer or even a link to a page or a site that explains the concept clearly, I would be something for me, as I can't find this precise information...

Thank you

True, Bitcoin is only semi-anonymous. There are ways to make yourself fully anonymous but in general if your Id can be linked to your address then someone could track you if they wanted to. To be anonymous you'd have to buy your coins in cash or do some sort of coin mixing, and there are a few other more esoteric ways that I won't get into because of the long explanation.

There are teams working on improving privacy. DarkWallet and Samourai Wallet are promising, they having different approaches though. But the general idea is to include automatic obfuscation of your coins when you send or receive. Both are still under development.

There are a few ways to anonymize your coins. Assuming you've purchased your coins through Coinbase, first transfer them to a blockchain.info wallet. Then you can simply use the Shared Send feature to make it difficult to reliably identify with confidence exactly where they came from. If you're really concerned you can do this more than once (to your own addresses) before finally sending them to their destination. (Note that at this moment the Shared Send feature isn't working very well due to the transaction level on the network - you might have to try a few times.) Blockchain.info has a TOR hidden service for the truly paranoid. https://blockchainbdgpzk.onion

There are also coin mixing services that will completely and totally sever any connection between you and the address you're sending to, however it's likely that the coins will be obviously anonymous - the receiver might know that they are coming from a mixing service. The greatest problem with these services is that you are essentially sending money to someone and 'hoping' that they will send the same amount to whoever you're paying. The CoinJoin algorithm used by blockchain.info's Shared Send feature requires no trust. The most popular appears to be BitBlender at http://bitblendervrfkzr.onion There's some helpful info there about anonymizing your coins as well.

A third option is to open an account at a bitcoin/USD exchange, like BTCe. (or another one that allows you to use any identity you choose.) Transfer some bits to your account and then withdraw them to an anonymous wallet. Just as with the mixers, you're trusting that the exchange won't go Gox on you while they have your money.

Personally, I use the first option.
